Jordan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: conversational analytics assistant over structured and semi-structured data (templates + user prompts).
- Estimated traffic shape: initial pilot ~10-20M raw tokens/month, seasonal spikes possible.
- Goal: land at an effective cost that fits their procurement target (~$300-$400 per 1M raw tokens).

Caching & pricing assumptions we discussed:
- Prefix / template caching expected to be high-impact since many prompts share identical instruction + few variable tokens.
- Typical prefix-cache hit-rate range (pilot): 40-70% depending on prompt diversity and personalization.
- List reference for model pricing we used in examples: $1,200 per 1M billable tokens (model-dependent; discounts apply).

Immediate follow-ups / asks:
1) Jordan: can you share a 48-72h sample of anonymized prompt logs (headers + templates) so we can run a quick cache-hit simulation?
2) Acme: confirm the budget range you mentioned on the call (you said a procurement target number — want to put on the MAP).
3) Redwood: we will provide a short pricing breakdown showing how different cache-hit scenarios (50/60/70%) affect effective $/1M raw tokens and an updated mutual action plan (attached).

Attachments: MAP (mutual action plan) + pricing breakdown CSV + short playbook for prefix caching.

If that all looks right I'll follow up with Marcus to run the simulation and propose a follow-up slot later this week.

- Procurement target: our head of procurement suggested a working target of $10k-$12k/mo for the pilot line item. Given our expected starting volume (~15M/month) that maps to roughly $666-$800 per 1M raw tokens.

Jordan — thanks for the extra color. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the figures discussed; below are three scenarios to illustrate how prefix caching affects the effective cost per 1M raw tokens. I'll run the simulation against your logs when you send them and attach a CSV with the breakdown (attached).

Assumptions used (example):
- Raw monthly tokens: 20,000,000 (we used a mid-point for illustration).
- Model list price (billable tokens): $1,200 per 1M tokens. (note: final quote may include volume/commit discounts)
- Prefix cache hit-rate scenarios: 50%, 60%, 70%

Raw cost (no caching): 20M / 1M * $1,200 = $24,000/month

With caching:
- 50% hit: billable tokens = 20M * (1 - 0.50) = 10M -> cost = 10 * $1,200 = $12,000 -> effective cost per 1M raw tokens = $12,000 / 20 = $600
- 60% hit: billable tokens = 8M -> cost = $9,600 -> effective cost per 1M raw tokens = $480
- 70% hit: billable tokens = 6M -> cost = $7,200 -> effective cost per 1M raw tokens = $360

Key takeaways:
- To reach your target band ($300-$400 per 1M raw tokens) at a $1,200 list price we need ~65-75% prefix-cache hit rate or additional pricing concessions (reserved capacity / committed volume).
- If we can push model choice to a smaller-but-acceptable variant or get a committed-reserved discount (example: 30-40% off list), the required cache hit target drops substantially. Example: 30% discount + 60% cache hit -> effective cost = 8M * $840 = $6,720 -> $6,720 / 20 = $336 per 1M raw tokens.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send a 48-72h anonymized sample of prompt logs (we'll only look at prompt text/keys) — we'll run a cache-simulation and give a more accurate hit-rate estimate.
2) If hit-rate is <60%, we'll model a blended approach (smaller model, cache, and a reserved commit discount) and show the MAP price bands.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next Wed/Thu to review the simulation and draft MAP.

I've attached a CSV with the numeric scenarios and the MAP doc Marissa referenced. Let me know what time works for the follow-up.

Thanks,
